faqBasics.question: What does QR Studio do?
faqBasics.answer: QR Studio turns any URL into a QR code you can style, save, and download. Sign up, paste a link, pick colors and size, optionally add a centre logo, then manage all your codes from one dashboard.

faqBasics.question: What types of QR codes can I create?
faqBasics.answer: Version one supports URL QR codes only — website links, landing pages, social profiles, or any https:// address. WiFi, vCard, email, and other payload types are not in this release.

faqBasics.question: Do I need an account?
faqBasics.answer: Yes. Create a free account with email and password to generate QR codes, save them to your library, and download PNG or SVG files whenever you need them.

faqBasics.question: Is QR Studio free?
faqBasics.answer: Yes. There are no paid plans in version one — create and manage as many QR codes as you need at no cost.

faqDesign.question: Can I edit my QR codes after creating them?
faqDesign.answer: Yes. Open any saved code from your dashboard to change the title, destination URL, foreground and background colors, output size, or centre logo. The image is regenerated from your updated settings.

faqDesign.question: Can I customize colors and add my logo?
faqDesign.answer: Yes. Pick foreground and background colors, set the output size, and upload a PNG, JPG, or SVG logo for the centre. Logos use high error correction so the code stays scannable.

faqDesign.question: Is there a limit to how many QR codes I can create?
faqDesign.answer: No. QR Studio is free and unlimited in version one — create as many codes as your projects need.

faqDesign.question: Can I download PNG and SVG?
faqDesign.answer: Yes. Every code can be downloaded as PNG for print and social use, or as SVG for crisp scaling. Both formats include your styling and embedded logo when you add one.

faqScanning.question: Will my QR code still scan with a logo in the center?
faqScanning.answer: Yes. QR Studio generates codes at error-correction level H and keeps the logo to roughly a quarter of the code width, leaving enough data for phone cameras and scanner apps to read reliably.

faqScanning.question: Can I add a QR code to my website?
faqScanning.answer: Yes. Download PNG or SVG and embed it on your site, in email, or on print materials. Anyone who scans the image goes to the destination URL you saved.

faqScanning.question: What happens if I change the destination URL?
faqScanning.answer: Editing the URL updates the saved code and regenerates the image. You will need to replace any printed or published files with the new download — this is not a dynamic redirect that changes where an old image points without reprinting.

faqScanning.question: How large should I print a QR code?
faqScanning.answer: Bigger is easier to scan. For posters and packaging, use the PNG download at your chosen size (up to 512 px by default) and scale up in your design tool while keeping sharp edges. Test with your phone before final print runs.
